source.title: Neutral harness design checks
source.checked: Verify controls against the target process and available evidence.
source.marks: These design checks do not replace evidence, authorisation, approval or the production prohibition.

think.label: Think
think.purpose: Break down messy problems and find the answer fast.

decide.label: Decide
decide.purpose: Make clear, fast calls and know who owns them.

situations.write: Write an email, memo or deck

frameworks.name: Coverage and overlap review
frameworks.what: Check that the proposed capabilities cover the agreed process without assigning the same responsibility twice.
frameworks.when: Use when dividing a process into outcomes or Talents.
steps: List the activities inside the agreed scope.
Assign each activity to one primary capability.
Identify duplicated responsibilities and uncovered activities.
Resolve each gap or overlap with the process owner.
frameworks.example: A request process separates intake, assessment and decision recording.
frameworks.watch_out: Coverage does not prove runtime enforcement.
frameworks.origin: General design guidance for this skill; no company affiliation or endorsement is asserted.

frameworks.name: Decision risk and frequency review
frameworks.what: Choose review controls from consequence, repetition and uncertainty.
frameworks.when: Use before proposing a harness level.
steps: Describe the decision and its possible consequences.
Record how often it occurs and whether the evidence varies.
Identify the human owner and the approval required.
Propose authority within the skill’s existing harness rules.
frameworks.habit: Reassess authority when consequences or inputs change.
frameworks.example: A recurring formatting choice may need fewer checks than an exceptional financial commitment.
frameworks.watch_out: Frequent decisions can still require human approval.
frameworks.origin: General design guidance for this skill; no company affiliation or endorsement is asserted.

frameworks.name: Reversibility review
frameworks.what: Evaluate recovery before assigning execution authority.
frameworks.when: Use when an action could change external state.
steps: Describe the state change and who it affects.
Identify a tested recovery route and its limits.
Record recovery cost, delay and any lasting consequences.
Escalate consequential or inadequately recoverable actions.
frameworks.habit: Check the recovery route before each new action class.
frameworks.example: A local draft can be revised; a signed commitment can create lasting obligations.
frameworks.watch_out: Reversibility alone does not grant permission.
frameworks.origin: General design guidance for this skill; no company affiliation or endorsement is asserted.

frameworks.name: Responsibility and decision ownership
frameworks.what: Name who performs the task, owns its result and makes its decisions.
frameworks.when: Use when defining responsibilities or escalation.
steps: Name the role that prepares or performs the work.
Name one accountable owner for the result.
Identify the assigned human decision maker where required.
List the roles consulted before a decision and informed afterward.
Specify an escalation recipient and timeout.
frameworks.habit: Review ownership when roles or process boundaries change.
frameworks.example: An analyst prepares an assessment, a designated reviewer decides, and the case owner records the receipt.
frameworks.watch_out: Role labels are not identity verification or approval evidence.
frameworks.origin: General design guidance for this skill; no company affiliation or endorsement is asserted.
